title: LinkedList, protocol-complete
prompt: Implement Node and LinkedList per the checkpoint specification: len, iteration, membership, repr 'LinkedList(1 -> 2 -> 3)', int indexing with negatives, slicing to a new LinkedList (with step), O(1) prepend, non-mutating reverse, and __slots__ on both classes.

tests.name: construction, len, iter, repr
tests.code:
l = LinkedList([1, 2, 3])
assert len(l) == 3
assert list(l) == [1, 2, 3]
assert repr(l) == 'LinkedList(1 -> 2 -> 3)'
assert LinkedList() .__len__() == 0
assert 2 in l and 99 not in l
print('ok')
tests.hint: Iterate nodes from _head; build repr with ' -> '.join(repr(v)).

tests.name: indexing with negatives and slices
tests.code:
l = LinkedList([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
assert l[0] == 1 and l[4] == 5 and l[-1] == 5 and l[-2] == 4
s = l[1:3]
assert isinstance(s, LinkedList) and list(s) == [2, 3]
st = l[0:5:2]
assert list(st) == [1, 3, 5]
try:
    l[99]
except IndexError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('out-of-range must raise IndexError')
print('ok')
tests.hint: slice.indices(len(self)) converts a slice to concrete bounds; handle negative ints before scanning.

tests.name: prepend, reverse, slots
tests.code:
l = LinkedList([2, 3])
l.prepend(1)
assert list(l) == [1, 2, 3]
r = l.reverse()
assert list(r) == [3, 2, 1] and list(l) == [1, 2, 3]
assert not hasattr(l, '__dict__') and not hasattr(Node(1), '__dict__')
print('ok')
tests.hint: reverse() must not mutate the original — build a new list by prepending.
